mainTopic: Splitting the two days of יום טוב: רבי יהודה's three cases, the basket-of-טבל condition, and the deer at the ריש גלותא's house
overview: This עמוד first finishes the view of the רבנן: the holiness of the first day in that case is only rabbinic, so people will not treat the day lightly. Then the גמרא explains why רבי יהודה needed three examples: ערוב, a basket of טבל, and an egg. Each one has its own reason we might have thought he would agree with the רבנן. Next, a ברייתא shows how the basket method works. On each of the two days he declares תרומה with a condition, so it takes effect on whichever day is a weekday. רבי יוסי forbids this, even on the two ימים טובים של גליות. A story follows about a deer brought to the ריש גלותא: רב נחמן and רב חסדא ate it, but רב ששת refused, citing איסי's version of רבי יוסי. רבא and רב אסי each try to reread איסי's words. Then רבה בר שמואל reports a ברייתא in which רבי יוסי agrees to be lenient on the Diaspora days. The עמוד ends as רב אשי begins אמימר's account that the deer was not trapped on יום טוב at all, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The רבנן's reason: so people will not take the day lightly
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that in that case the holiness of the first day is only rabbinic. It was set up so people would not come to treat the day lightly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: there, it was only so that people would not treat the day lightly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining the view of the רבנן, which began on the previous עמוד. It explains why the רבנן treat this case as they do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that case, the day was kept holy because of a rabbinic decree, not because of תורה law. The goal was that people should not come to belittle the day in later years. Since by תורה law it is really an ordinary day, the two days are not one single holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, who argue with רבי יהודה here

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of an answer that started on the previous עמוד. It is not a brand-new statement, so read it as finishing the earlier discussion.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: there,
phrases.notes: Refers to the case discussed on the previous amud

phrases.english: it was so that people would not treat it lightly.
phrases.notes: The holiness of that day is a rabbinic safeguard

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, הָתָם כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לְזַלְזוֹלֵי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an explanation that began in the earlier part of the daf
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reason behind the רבנן's position
steps.terutzMaskana: In that case the day's holiness is only rabbinic, meant to stop people from belittling it

steps.title: Quoting the next line of the משנה about רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: 'And רבי יהודה said further...', which brings in the cases of the basket and the egg.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה to set up a new discussion. This line is a setup for the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, after his ruling about ערוב on ראש השנה, רבי יהודה adds two more cases. The first is a basket of טבל. The second is an egg laid on the first day. In all of them he treats the two days as separate.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the rest of the quote is left out
The תנא who rules that the two days of ראש השנה can be split

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda said further
etc.
phrases.notes: Points to the basket and egg cases

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רבנן's reasoning to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה applies his splitting of the two days to more cases

steps.title: Why the basket case was needed after ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says all the cases are needed. From the ערוב case alone, we might think רבי יהודה would agree with the רבנן about the basket, since that case looks like fixing טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was necessary to teach all of them. If he had only taught us ראש השנה, we would say רבי יהודה rules this way only there, because the person does not actually do anything. But with a basket, which looks like fixing טבל, we would say he agrees with the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a צריכותא, explaining why רבי יהודה needed more than one example. Here it shows why the basket case could not be learned from the ערוב case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ערוב, the person does no action on יום טוב, so being lenient is easy. With the basket, he declares תרומה with a condition on each of the two days. That looks like fixing טבל on יום טוב, which is forbidden. So we might have thought רבי יהודה would be strict there, and he had to say otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was necessary to teach each case

steps.confusionAlert: A צריכותא is not a challenge. The גמרא is not attacking רבי יהודה. It is explaining why he needed several examples to make his view clear.

phrases.english: And it is necessary.
For if he had taught us only Rosh Hashana,
only in this case does Rabbi Yehuda say it,
because he does not do anything.
phrases.notes: No action is done on יום טוב

phrases.english: But a basket,
which looks like fixing tevel,
phrases.notes: Fixing טבל on יום טוב is forbidden

phrases.english: I would say he agrees with the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the cases quoted from the משנה are all needed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The basket case is needed because it looks like fixing טבל, unlike ערוב, where no action is done

steps.title: Why the egg case was needed after the first two
steps.stepSummary: From the first two cases, we might think רבי יהודה would agree with the רבנן about the egg. The egg has its own rabbinic decrees: fruit that falls and liquids that ooze. So all three cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had taught us only these two, we would say it is because there is no reason to make a decree about them. But an egg, where there is reason to make a decree because of fruit that falls and liquids that ooze, I would say he agrees with the רבנן. So it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא by showing why the egg case could not be learned from the first two. It then concludes that all three were needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ערוב and the basket, there is no special decree to worry about. But an egg laid on יום טוב is similar to fruit that fell or liquids that oozed on יום טוב, which חז״ל forbade. So we might have thought רבי יהודה would be strict about the egg, and he had to teach otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: An egg laid on יום טוב
Fruit that falls from a tree
Liquids that oozed out of fruit

steps.whatToRemember: Each of רבי יהודה's three cases adds something new. ערוב involves no action. The basket looks like fixing טבל. The egg is linked to other rabbinic decrees. In every case he still holds that the two days of ראש השנה can be split.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how firm רבי יהודה's view is. Even in the cases where we would most expect him to be strict, he still treats the two days as separate.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only these two,
it would be because there is no reason to decree about them.
But an egg, where there is reason to decree,
because of fruit that falls
and because of liquids that oozed,
I would say he agrees with the Rabbis;
so it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the צריכותא begun in step 3
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three cases were needed because each has its own reason why רבי יהודה might have agreed with the רבנן

steps.title: How the basket condition works on the first day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains רבי יהודה's method. On the first day, the person makes a condition over two baskets of טבל so that one becomes תרומה for the other only if today is a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: How does רבי יהודה's rule work, that a person makes a condition on a basket on the first day of יום טוב and eats it on the second? If he had two baskets of טבל in front of him, he says: 'If today is a weekday and tomorrow is holy, let this one be תרומה for that one. If today is holy and tomorrow is a weekday, my words mean nothing.' He calls it by the name תרומה and puts it aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that spells out, step by step, what a person actually does on day one under רבי יהודה's rule about the basket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separating תרומה is not allowed on יום טוב, but it is allowed on a weekday. We do not know which of the two days is really holy, so the person makes his words count only if today is the weekday. If today turns out to be holy, nothing happened, so he did no forbidden act.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Produce from which תרומה and מעשרות have not yet been taken; forbidden to eat
My words mean nothing (the condition does not take effect)
He calls it by a name (declares it תרומה)

steps.confusionAlert: He is not separating תרומה on יום טוב. His words only take effect if today turns out to be a regular weekday.

phrases.english: It was taught: How did Rabbi Yehuda say
a person makes a condition about the basket
on the first day of the Festival and eats it on the second?

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁתֵּי כַּלְכַּלּוֹת שֶׁל טֶבֶל,
phrases.english: If there were before him two baskets of tevel,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמֵר: אִם הַיּוֹם חוֹל וּלְמָחָר קֹדֶשׁ —
phrases.english: he says: If today is a weekday and tomorrow is holy,
let this one be teruma for that one,
and if today is holy and tomorrow is a weekday,
my words mean nothing.
And he calls it by the name (teruma), and sets it aside.
phrases.notes: He does not eat yet. He waits for the second day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing that all three cases of רבי יהודה are needed, the גמרא now explains how the basket case actually works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On day one, he makes the תרומה conditional on today being a weekday. He declares it and sets the basket aside.

steps.title: Repeating the condition on the second day and eating
steps.stepSummary: On the second day, he repeats the condition the other way. Now one of the two days was surely a weekday, so the תרומה is surely separated and he may eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next day he says: 'If today is a weekday, let this one be תרומה for that one. If today is holy, my words mean nothing.' He calls it by the name תרומה and eats.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the procedure. On the second day he repeats the same condition, and then he is allowed to eat the produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One of the two days must be a weekday. So either yesterday's words worked or today's words worked. Either way, the תרומה was separated on a weekday, and the rest of the basket is no longer טבל.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן; separating it fixes the טבל

steps.whatToRemember: The trick works because one of the two days is surely a weekday, so one of the two declarations must take effect.

phrases.english: And the next day he says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הַיּוֹם חוֹל — תְּהֵא זוֹ תְּרוּמָה עַל זוֹ,
phrases.english: If today is a weekday, let this one be teruma for that one,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הַיּוֹם קֹדֶשׁ — אֵין בִּדְבָרַי כְּלוּם.
phrases.english: and if today is holy, my words mean nothing.
And he calls it by the name (teruma) and eats it.
phrases.notes: He eats the other basket, which is now fixed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the procedure that began on day one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repeating the condition on day two makes sure the תרומה was separated on a weekday, so eating is allowed.

steps.title: רבי יוסי forbids, even for the two days kept outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי does not allow this condition. He forbids it even for the two ימים טובים של גליות, which are kept only out of doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי forbids it. And רבי יוסי would also forbid it on the two days of יום טוב kept in the Diaspora.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the opposing view. רבי יוסי says this procedure is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even outside ארץ ישראל, where the second day is kept only because of an old doubt about the date, רבי יוסי still forbids the condition. He treats both days as fully holy and does not let you play one day against the other.

keyTerms.meaning: The two days of יום טוב kept in the Diaspora

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling becomes the source רב שׁשׁת relies on in the story that follows.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei forbids.
And so too Rabbi Yosei would forbid
on the two Festival days of the Diaspora.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יהודה's procedure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי forbids the two-day condition, even for the Diaspora's two days of יום טוב.

steps.title: The deer brought to the house of the ריש גלותא
steps.stepSummary: A story: a deer was trapped on the first day of יום טוב in the Diaspora and slaughtered on the second day. The question is whether it may be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain young deer that came to the house of the ריש גלותא. It was trapped on the first day of יום טוב of the Diaspora and slaughtered on the second day of יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that tests the same idea in real life. It is setting up the question of who ate the deer and who did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Either the first day was the weekday, so the trapping was fine, or the second day was the weekday, so the slaughtering was fine. If we treat the two days as one being surely ordinary, like רבי יהודה, the deer should be allowed. If we follow רבי יוסי, it should not.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, leader of the Jews in Bavel

phrases.english: A certain young deer
that came to the house of the Exilarch

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִתְּצִיד בְּיוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל גָּלִיּוֹת,
phrases.english: which was trapped on the first Festival day of the Diaspora,
and was slaughtered on the second Festival day.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא בַּר טַבְיָא דַּאֲתָא לְבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא to a real case that raises the same issue of the two Diaspora days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case: trapped on day one, slaughtered on day two of יום טוב in the Diaspora.

steps.title: Two רבנן eat, רב שׁשׁת refuses, and רב נחמן teases him
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן and רב חסדא ate the deer, but רב שׁשׁת did not. רב נחמן jokingly asks what to do with רב שׁשׁת, who will not eat deer meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן and רב חסדא ate. רב שׁשׁת did not eat. רב נחמן said: What can I do for רב שׁשׁת, who does not eat deer meat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports who ate and who did not. רב נחמן lightly challenges רב שׁשׁת for being strict, which sets up רב שׁשׁת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן and רב חסדא held that one of the two days is surely a weekday, so the meat is allowed. רב נחמן's joke really means: why are you being strict when there is no reason to forbid it?

keyTerms.meaning: What can I do for him? (a teasing remark)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman and Rav Chisda ate,
Rav Sheshet did not eat.
Rav Nachman said:
What can I do for Rav Sheshet
who does not eat deer meat?
phrases.notes: Said as a joke, but it challenges his strictness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports how the חכמים acted on the deer case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שׁשׁת's refusal to eat the deer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One of the two days was surely a weekday, so the deer should be allowed. Why be strict?

steps.title: רב שׁשׁת cites איסי's teaching of רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב שׁשׁת explains that he cannot eat, because איסי taught that רבי יוסי forbids this even on the two ימים טובים של גליות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שׁשׁת said to him: How can I eat, when איסי taught (and some say it is a question: didn't איסי teach?): 'And so too רבי יוסי would forbid it on the two days of יום טוב of the Diaspora!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב שׁשׁת answers רב נחמן's tease by pointing to a source that backs up his strictness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שׁשׁת relies on the same line we saw in the ברייתא, as taught by איסי: רבי יוסי treats the two Diaspora days as holy and will not split them. If so, the deer, which was trapped on one day and slaughtered on the next, stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who taught this ברייתא
And some say it (another version of the line)

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן and רב חסדא treated the two Diaspora days as 'one is surely a weekday.' רב שׁשׁת followed רבי יוסי, who forbids such reasoning even for the Diaspora days.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to him:
And how can I eat, since Isi taught,
and some say it as a question, 'Didn't Isi teach':
And so too Rabbi Yosei would forbid
the two Festival days of the Diaspora!

steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a source (a ברייתא of איסי) to justify the strict practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב שׁשׁת was being strict for no reason, since one of the days was surely a weekday
steps.terutzMaskana: רב שׁשׁת follows רבי יוסי, who forbids such reasoning even on the Diaspora's two days of יום טוב

steps.title: רבא rereads איסי's teaching as speaking about ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא suggests that איסי's teaching is only about the two days of ראש השנה in the Diaspora. So it does not prove that רבי יוסי forbids on other Diaspora יום טוב days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the difficulty? Maybe this is what איסי meant: רבי יוסי would also forbid this on the two days of ראש השנה in the Diaspora.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב ששת's proof. He says איסי's words can be read in a narrower way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת read איסי as saying רבי יוסי forbids on all the Diaspora festival days. רבא says איסי may only mean ראש השנה, which has special stringency. On regular festivals, רבי יוסי might permit, and then the deer would be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difficulty? A phrase that rejects a supposed proof or problem
Perhaps this is what he meant: introduces a different reading
The New Year festival, which has two days even in ארץ ישראל
In the Diaspora, outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rava said: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps this is what he meant:
And so too, Rabbi Yosei would forbid

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בַּגּוֹלָה!
phrases.english: on the two festival days of Rosh Hashana in the Diaspora!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וּמַאי קוּשְׁיָא? דִּילְמָא הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof רב ששת drew from איסי's teaching in step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not איסי's teaching itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: איסי's words could refer only to ראש השנה in the Diaspora, not to all the Diaspora festival days

steps.title: The wording 'of the Diaspora' does not fit רבא's reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's reading from איסי's wording. If איסי meant ראש השנה in the Diaspora, he should have said 'in the Diaspora,' not 'of the Diaspora.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, instead of saying 'of the Diaspora,' he should have said 'in the Diaspora'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's reading by looking closely at איסי's exact words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'ימים טובים של גליות' names a type of festival day: the extra days that exist only because of the Diaspora. ראש השנה's two days are not that type, since they exist even in ארץ ישראל. So איסי's wording points to the regular Diaspora festival days, and רבא's reading fails.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a problem with the last suggestion
Of the Diaspora: festival days that belong to the Diaspora, kept only there

steps.confusionAlert: 'של גליות' and 'בגולה' sound almost the same, but they mean different things. 'של גליות' describes a kind of day that exists only because of the Diaspora. 'בגולה' only tells you where something happens.

phrases.english: If so, instead of "of the Diaspora"
he should have said "in the Diaspora"!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's suggestion that איסי meant ראש השנה in the Diaspora
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The precise wording 'של גליות' refers to the Diaspora-only festival days, not to ראש השנה days that happen to be in the Diaspora

steps.title: רב אסי rereads איסי's teaching as actually lenient
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי offers another reading. רבי יוסי treats the Diaspora festival days like ראש השנה as the רבנן see it, and the רבנן permit. So איסי's teaching may actually be lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: What is the difficulty? Maybe this is what איסי meant: רבי יוסי would treat the rule for the two Diaspora festival days the same as the two days of ראש השנה according to the רבנן, who permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי gives a second, different way to read איסי, so that it no longer supports רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי keeps the words 'של גליות,' so he avoids the problem from step 12. He changes the meaning instead. רבי יוסי compares the Diaspora days to ראש השנה according to the רבנן, who allow the two-way תנאי there. On this reading, איסי's teaching is a leniency, and eating the deer would be fine.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps this is what he meant:

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי עוֹשֶׂה אִיסּוּר
phrases.english: And so too, Rabbi Yosei would treat the law
of the two festival days of the Diaspora

phrases.aramaic: כִּשְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
phrases.english: like the two festival days of Rosh Hashana
according to the Rabbis, who permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: וּמַאי קוּשְׁיָא? דִּילְמָא הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's reading was rejected, רב אסי offers a new reading that fits the wording 'של גליות'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב ששת's proof from איסי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: איסי's comparison may be to the lenient view of the רבנן on ראש השנה, which makes it a leniency rather than a stringency

steps.title: רב ששת asks רבה בר שמואל what he learned
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת meets רבה בר שמואל and asks whether he has learned any teaching about the 'two sanctities' of the festival days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת met רבה בר שמואל and said to him: Has the master learned anything about the sanctities of the festival days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a follow-up story. רב ששת asks another scholar for any teaching on this topic, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת wants to check whether there is another teaching about the two days and whether they count as one holiness or two. This question opens a new source on the issue.

keyTerms.meaning: Has the master learned anything? (a request for a ברייתא)
Sanctities: whether the two festival days are two separate holinesses or one

phrases.aramaic: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לְרַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet met Rabba bar Shmuel,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תָּנֵי מָר מִידֵּי בִּקְדוּשּׁוֹת?
phrases.english: and said to him: Has the master learned anything about the sanctities?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לְרַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the debate over איסי's wording and opens a story about another teaching
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבה בר שמואל knows a ברייתא about the sanctities of the two festival days

steps.title: רבי יוסי agrees to be lenient on the Diaspora festival days
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל answers with a teaching that רבי יוסי agrees, and permits, on the two ימים טובים של גליות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We learned: רבי יוסי agrees about the two festival days of the Diaspora.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שמואל answers. He quotes a teaching that says רבי יוסי is lenient on the Diaspora days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching goes directly against איסי's version, which said רבי יוסי forbids even on the Diaspora days. 'מודה' means רבי יוסי agrees with the lenient view there. So it supports רב נחמן and רב חסדא, who ate the deer.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, concedes to the other view (here, to permit)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'מודה' as 'agrees to forbid.' It means רבי יוסי gives in to the lenient side here. That is the opposite of what איסי said.

phrases.english: He said to him: We have learned:
Rabbi Yosei agrees
regarding the two festival days of the Diaspora.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ תְּנֵינָא: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's question from step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא that רבי יוסי permits the two-way תנאי on the Diaspora festival days
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a ברייתא, a source from the time of the תנאים, that goes against איסי. It backs up the leniency of רב נחמן and רב חסדא.

steps.title: רב ששת asks him not to tell the others
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת asks רבה בר שמואל not to tell רב נחמן and רב חסדא anything about this teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If you meet them, do not tell them anything.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת reacts to the teaching and asks that it not be passed on to the rabbis who ate the deer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching supports רב נחמן and רב חסדא against רב ששת's refusal to eat. רב ששת does not want them to use it to tease him or embarrass him. This shows he saw the teaching as a real challenge to his position.

keyTerms.meaning: If you happen to meet them

steps.whatToRemember: There are two conflicting reports of רבי יוסי's view on the Diaspora days. איסי says he forbids. רבה בר שמואל's ברייתא says he agrees to permit.

phrases.english: He said to him: If you meet them,
do not tell them anything at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לְהוּ, לָא תֵּימָא לְהוּ וְלָא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב ששת's reaction to the teaching quoted in step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת recognizes that the ברייתא supports the rabbis who ate the deer, and asks that it not be told to them

steps.title: אמימר's version: the deer was not trapped on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports a different version of the deer story from אמימר. The deer was not trapped on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: אמימר told me himself: that deer was not trapped on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the deer story from step 8 with a new version of the facts. This line sets up an explanation that continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, everyone assumed the deer was trapped on the first day, so רבי יוסי's ruling on the two Diaspora days mattered. אמימר says the deer was not trapped on יום טוב at all. This changes why it may have been permitted. The full explanation continues on the next עמוד.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לְדִידִי אֲמַר לִי אַמֵּימָר:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Ameimar told me personally:
That deer
was not trapped (on the festival) at all,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לְדִידִי אֲמַר לִי אַמֵּימָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the deer story from step 8 with a different version of the facts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אמימר, the deer was not trapped on יום טוב (the statement continues on the next amud)
